```python
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("MultiObjective_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 5  # sources
    J = 11  # destinations
    K = 3  # max suppliers per store
    w_cost = 0.6
    w_emission = 0.4

    supplies = [116, 126, 228, 142, 181]
    demands = [45, 38, 57, 29, 22, 56, 53, 21, 40, 41, 20]
    cost_matrix = [[26.94, 16.56, 29.49, 11.78, 3.11, 13.87, 19.25, 7.47, 23.52, 16.84, 21.53], [14.99, 18.14, 28.36, 21.53, 13.11, 21.78, 16.25, 19.54, 19.32, 25.15, 27.73], [18.37, 20.11, 8.46, 18.17, 7.95, 12.19, 10.89, 26.3, 20.49, 7.5, 4.72], [10.8, 19.8, 27.45, 17.41, 5.04, 23.3, 24.33, 28.53, 21.76, 26.5, 26.24], [29.81, 7.76, 24.44, 14.64, 19.05, 14.28, 16.18, 12.25, 25.73, 26.84, 10.67]]
    emission_matrix = [[9.11, 12.26, 8.41, 5.8, 8.69, 16.77, 5.87, 14.04, 16.18, 4.68, 4.54], [15.27, 5.22, 15.04, 14.01, 10.7, 10.86, 10.45, 5.3, 11.23, 16.53, 13.25], [15.89, 5.06, 12.82, 17.8, 20.0, 4.76, 19.43, 12.88, 4.51, 16.95, 16.44], [14.5, 4.43, 12.15, 17.4, 14.61, 11.09, 11.83, 5.56, 6.6, 5.23, 6.08], [1.0, 17.37, 4.42, 17.18, 2.63, 12.89, 16.48, 6.12, 7.48, 14.86, 19.75]]
    fixed_costs = [[206, 263, 273, 198, 207, 295, 92, 198, 280, 104, 58], [270, 213, 52, 292, 298, 171, 59, 287, 296, 181, 179], [177, 217, 243, 200, 182, 66, 173, 230, 80, 137, 191], [294, 202, 171, 287, 90, 120, 81, 174, 186, 247, 253], [290, 132, 271, 225, 193, 215, 126, 72, 257, 117, 159]]
    moq = [[20, 7, 18, 19, 14, 20, 9, 19, 16, 7, 20], [9, 16, 14, 19, 13, 14, 7, 5, 20, 7, 6], [7, 9, 15, 14, 16, 6, 16, 15, 6, 13, 8], [14, 15, 11, 7, 18, 12, 18, 20, 16, 7, 9], [15, 16, 7, 13, 15, 8, 15, 12, 12, 17, 17]]

    # Big-M per route
    total_demand = sum(demands)
    big_M = [[min(supplies[i], total_demand) for j in range(J)] for i in range(I)]

    # --- Variables ---
    # Continuous: shipment quantities
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Ship_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Binary: route-open indicators
    y = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            y[(i,j)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"RouteOpen_S{i}_D{j}")

    # --- Objective ---
    # Weighted variable cost + fixed setup costs
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(
            (w_cost * cost_matrix[i][j] + w_emission * emission_matrix[i][j]) * x[(i,j)]
            for i in range(I) for j in range(J)
        )
        + quicksum(fixed_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"Supply_S{i}")

    # C2: Demand
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) >= demands[j],
            name=f"Demand_D{j}")

    # C3: Linking — can only ship if route is open
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] <= big_M[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"Link_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C4: Minimum order quantity
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            m.addConstr(
                x[(i,j)] >= moq[i][j] * y[(i,j)],
                name=f"MOQ_S{i}_D{j}")

    # C5: Max suppliers per store
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(y[(i,j)] for i in range(I)) <= K,
            name=f"MaxSupplier_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m
```

To: Executive Leadership Team
From: Sustainability & Logistics Director
Date: [Insert Date]
Subject: Balanced Shipping Plan for Cost and Carbon Impact Across Our Warehouse-to-Store Network

Context
Our multi-warehouse, multi-store network ships products on routes that carry two metrics per unit moved: monetary cost and carbon emissions. In practice, the cheapest lanes often have higher emissions intensity, while cleaner options can be more expensive. We need a plan that balances spend discipline with our sustainability commitments while maintaining service reliability.

Operational Rules
To reflect how our operations actually run, the shipping plan must respect the following:
- Route activation and setup fees: Opening a lane requires a one-time setup charge covering contracts, compliance, and dock readiness. A lane is either active or inactive. If inactive, no volume or setup charge applies; if active, the setup fee is incurred regardless of volume.
- Minimum order quantities per active lane: Once a lane is activated, we must move at least a specified minimum volume on it to justify trucking, loading, and handling. Partial loads below that threshold are not accepted.
- Supplier limits per store: Each store can receive from only a limited number of warehouses in a period to manage receiving dock capacity, scheduling, and vendor complexity.

Supply and Demand
The plan must respect available inventory at each warehouse and meet the minimum demand requirements at each store. No warehouse should be planned to ship more than it has available, and no store should be left short against its requirement.

Management Priority
Leadership has defined a weighted balance between cost and emissions. We will score plans by:
- Weighting the total variable shipping cost by the cost importance,
- Weighting the total emissions by the emissions importance,
- Adding the full value of any route setup fees for lanes we activate (these one-time fees are not weighted).
This creates a clear, consistent yardstick for comparing options across all feasible lane combinations and shipment allocations.

Business Goal
Identify which lanes to activate and how much to move on each active lane so that:
- Warehouse supply limits are respected,
- Store demand is fully served,
- Any activated lane meets its minimum order quantity,
- Each store receives from no more than the allowed number of supplying warehouses,
- The blended score of weighted variable cost, weighted total emissions, and full setup fees is as low as possible.
The resulting plan should be operationally executable, financially prudent, and aligned with our sustainability targets. We will prepare alternative scenarios to illustrate trade-offs across the defined cost and carbon weights and highlight lanes where setup charges and minimums drive meaningful differences.
